chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from Asim ibn Hamid, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: May God have mercy on the sisters from the people of Paradise, and he named them: Asma' bint Umays al-Khas'amiyyah, who was under the marriage of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him); and Salmi bint Umays al-Khas'amiyyah, who was under the marriage of Hamzah; and five from Banu Hilal: Maymuna bint al-Harith, who was under the marriage of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family); and Umm al-Fadl with al-Abbas, her name was Hind; and al-Ghumaysha', mother of Khalid ibn al-Walid; and 'Azzah, who was in Thaqif, al-Hajjaj ibn Ghalladh; and Hamida, and she had no offspring.
ai.seo_question: Who are the seven sisters of the Prophet mentioned in Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) identifying seven specific women as the 'sisters' of the Prophet (PBUH) in Paradise, a title denoting their close spiritual and familial bond. The list notably includes Asma' and Salmi bint Umays, who were married to the Prophet's cousins Jafar and Hamza, alongside five other women from the Banu Hilal tribe, highlighting the intertribal and familial networks that supported early Islam. This enumeration serves to validate the high status of these women within Shia tradition, emphasizing their piety and connection to the Ahl al-Bayt.
